text: @sysit/dsh-remote-access 是一个 DSH Web profile bundle：它通过配置 webserver 的 host，让 DSH Web 界面可以使用环境变量指定监听地址。默认监听 127.0.0.1，也可通过 DSH_WEB_HOST 调整；服务端口沿用 webStartup 配置，缺省为 3080，并保留 gzip 压缩设置。安装到 web profile 后，补丁覆盖该 profile 中的 webserver 配置。适合希望从其他设备访问 DSH Web 界面的用户；使用时按需设置 DSH_WEB_HOST，不需要额外的 API 密钥或第三方服务。

@sysit/dsh-remote-access is a DSH web profile bundle that sets the webserver host from DSH_WEB_HOST (default 127.0.0.1). It retains the configured port and gzip settings. Install it in the web profile to choose the DSH Web UI bind address. No API key or external service is declared.
想从同一网络的另一台设备打开 DSH 的 Web 界面。
How can I choose which network address the DSH web interface listens on?
@sysit/dsh-remote-access 的功能「配置 Web 监听地址」：通过 DSH_WEB_HOST 设置 webserver host，默认值为 127.0.0.1。补丁应用于 web profile。

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · dsh-remote-access：Out-of-tree [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-harness) web-profile **bundle** that lets the `dsh --profile web` GUI listen on **all interfaces** (`0.0.0.0`) so you can open it from another device — while keeping the **built-in `?token=` BrowserAuth and never touching authentication**.

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · dsh-remote-access：It is intentionally tiny: **one `webserver` row**. Unlike earlier plugins, it does **not** fork `web-startup` / `webserver` / `connection` and does **not** invent its own token gate. That is precisely why it survives dsh upgrades: the auth and the LAN `?token=` URL printing already come from dsh itself; this bundle only lets `host` be non-loopback.

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · How it works：- dsh's `BrowserAuth` (`client/connection`) issues a **host-bound** cookie (`dsh-auth-<sha256(authority)>`) when you open the printed `?token=` URL. It already works for a LAN bind.
- `web-app` prints the LAN URL `(LAN: http://<ip>:<port>/?token=...)` whenever the server binds `0.0.0.0`.
- The only blocker in stock dsh is `web-startup` refusing `--host 0.0.0.0`. This bundle **does not unblock that flag**; instead it overrides the `webserver` row's `host` from an env var, so you never pass `--host`.
- Result: zero third-party, zero plugins that own the auth, and a **profile-level patch** the loader re-reads on every boot — so it needs no re-apply after a dsh upgrade.
@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · from a git checkout：dsh plugin --profile web install github:sysit/dsh-remote-access

section: or from a local path (e.g. while developing)

text:
@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · Use：| Want | Command |
|---|---|
| **Remote** (default when set) | `export DSH_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0 && dsh --profile web --no-open` |
| **Loopback only** | unset `DSH_WEB_HOST`, or `DSH_WEB_HOST=127.0.0.1 dsh --profile web` |
| launchd/KeepAlive | add `export DSH_WEB_HOST="\${DSH_WEB_HOST:-0.0.0.0}"` to the launch script |

On a remote bind the startup log prints both:

```
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=eqeU… (LAN: http://192.168.1.5:3080/?token=eqeU…)
```

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · Use：Open the `LAN:` URL on another device — no 401, no plugin auth, no relay. The token is **per-process** (changes each restart); the browser cookie is valid up to `cookieMaxAgeDays` (default 30 days), so an already-open tab keeps working across restarts.

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · Upgrade handling：Nothing to re-apply. The patch is a declarative layer in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/` (outside the dsh repo), re-read on every boot. After a dsh upgrade, smoke-check:

```sh
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.deepseek-ai.dsh-web   # restart your web service
tail -5 ~/Library/Logs/dsh/web.out.log                        # expect `?token=` + `(LAN: ...)`
```

If dsh ever renames the `webserver` row id or its config keys, regenerate the row from the current official patch:

@sysit/dsh-remote-access README · Upgrade handling：```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config                              # current webserver keys
cat packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml                  # official webserver row
```
